title: Signalizer: Lost Signal Finder
short: No signal? Follow the arrow back to the last place you had service. Offline.
hook_sub: When the signal drops, Signalizer points you back to the last place you had service.
c2_sub: The map turns with you. Distance and walking time to your last signal — GPS only, no network.

full:
You'll need it one day.

Signalizer remembers the last place your phone had cell signal — and when the signal drops, it brings you back to that last-signal point: your trail on a map that turns with you, a compass arrow, the exact distance and the walking time. An offline GPS compass that works with no internet and no network: in the desert, in the mountains, hiking, camping, anywhere with no signal.

100% offline. No internet. No account. No subscription. Total privacy — nothing ever leaves your phone.

LOST SIGNAL? WALK YOUR TRAIL BACK
• While you have signal, Signalizer quietly saves your GPS location — offline, no internet.
• Always watch (optional): turn it on once, and the moment the signal drops your GPS trail starts recording by itself — light on battery while you have coverage.
• Or tap "Heading out" before a desert trip or a hike. It watches your signal in the background and records your trail, even if you close the app. Tap "I’m back" when the network is back.
• No signal? Your trail is drawn on a map that turns with you, with the distance and walking time back to the last point with network — where you can call emergency services. Prefer the big compass arrow? Switch with one tap.
• One signal, one trail: each new signal loss starts one clear trail, never a confusing mess.

MARK YOUR PLACES
• "Mark this place" saves your car, your camp or a well. Later, a compass arrow with distance and walking time takes you back — offline, GPS only.
• Your places stay on your phone until you delete them. Total privacy.

AN EMERGENCY COMPASS FOR THE DESERT, THE MOUNTAINS AND THE OPEN ROAD
• Compass, bearing, distance and walking time from GPS only — offline, no network, no internet.
• Battery estimate: see roughly how many hours your battery will last while GPS is recording.
• Export your trail as a GPX file to share with rescuers or friends when you are back in coverage.
• Day mode readable in harsh desert sun, night mode for OLED screens, switching automatically at sunrise and sunset — computed from GPS, offline.
• The local emergency number for where you are, from GPS — offline.
• A short offline emergency guide: what to do when you're stranded in the desert or lost hiking with no signal, saving water and battery, distress signals for an emergency.
• Open the last-signal point or any marked place in any maps app you have.

NO INTERNET, 100% — TOTAL PRIVACY
Signalizer has no internet permission at all, so it cannot send anything — real privacy, not promises. Location, trail and places are stored only on your device and deleted when you uninstall. No ads, no tracking, no analytics, no account. Your privacy in the desert, in the mountains or in the city stays yours — offline.

WHY SIGNALIZER?
The first thing you lose in the desert or on a mountain hike is signal, and the first thing you need in an emergency is network. Signalizer is the emergency compass that brings you back to your last cell signal — an offline GPS compass, simple, private, and ready before you need it.

For everyone who heads into the desert, goes hiking or camping off-grid. One-time purchase. No subscription. No internet. Available in 46 languages.

FAQ
• Does it really work with no internet? Yes, 100% offline — there is no internet permission at all, and GPS works with no network.
• Does the compass need a network? No, the compass, distance and walking time come from GPS and the phone's sensors only.
• What happens in an emergency? Follow your trail or the emergency compass back to your last signal, then call emergency services as soon as the network is back.
• Privacy? Total privacy — offline, no account, no internet, and no data ever leaves your phone.
• Battery? Always watch uses low-power location while you have signal and full GPS only when the signal is weak or lost; "Heading out" uses GPS for one trip. The offline night mode saves battery too.
